QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: enabled
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: Control a SIYI optical pod (ZT30, ZT6, ZR30, ZR10, A8) directly over its own Ethernet link using the SIYI SDK protocol. The ground station must share a network with the camera. On this airframe a ZT30 is always fitted, so this is on by default; with no pod answering the controller simply reports it as disconnected. Video is configured separately under Video settings.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: Enable SIYI camera control

QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: ipAddress
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: IP address of the SIYI optical pod. The SIYI factory default is 192.168.144.25; on this airframe the pod is readdressed to 192.168.144.26 so the FPV camera can keep .25.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: Camera IP address

QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: port
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: UDP port the SIYI pod listens on for SDK commands. Factory default is 37260.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: Camera SDK port

QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: secondaryRtspUrl
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: RTSP URL for the ZT30 sub stream shown in the second camera panel. The pod publishes its main stream on /video1 and its sub stream on /video2; the path varies by camera firmware, so verify it on the installed payload.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: Secondary RTSP URL

QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: aiEnabled
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: Talk to a SIYI AI tracking module on its own Ethernet address. The module is separate hardware between the optical pod and the SIYI link; it recognises and tracks one selected target (person, car, bus, truck). Enabling it also moves the main video window onto the module's own RTSP feed, which is where tap-to-track has to happen: the target the operator picks is only meaningful in the frame the module itself sees, and a tap on the pod's own stream lands somewhere else in the module's picture. Off by default all the same, because on this airframe the module answers RTSP DESCRIBE but sends no media - turning it on before that is fixed replaces the working pod stream with a black window.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: Enable SIYI AI tracking module

QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: aiIpAddress
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: IP address of the SIYI AI tracking module. Factory default is 192.168.144.60.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: AI module IP address

QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: aiPort
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: UDP port the SIYI AI tracking module listens on. Factory default is 37260.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: AI module SDK port

QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: aiRtspUrl
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: RTSP stream carrying the AI recognition boxes. Verified on the actual Module II hardware: the module publishes this on its OWN address, port 554 - not on the pod's address the manual mirrors suggest. The pod's plain main/sub streams stay at the pod address. Which gimbal the module reads is set in setip.txt on its SD card (VideoAddress). Not yet playing on this airframe: the module answers DESCRIBE with 200 OK and takes SDK commands on UDP 37260, but no media follows and GStreamer retries every 11 s, while the pod's own streams and the FPV camera play in the same app.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: AI module RTSP URL

QGC.MetaData.Facts.name: fpvRtspUrl
QGC.MetaData.Facts.shortDesc: RTSP address of the FPV camera on the air unit LAN2 port.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.longDesc: RTSP address of the forward-looking FPV camera on the air unit's LAN2 port. Left empty the FPV window stays closed. On this airframe the FPV camera keeps the SIYI default 192.168.144.25 and the pod moved to .26; a third-party camera uses its own address. Probed on the airframe: this camera answers /main.264, and every video0/video1/video2 path 404s - those belong to the pod and the AI module.
QGC.MetaData.Facts.label: FPV camera RTSP URL
